storms.key_moments: KEY MOMENTS: shock 14:45 UT 15 Jul (6 -> 24 nPa) | Bz min -60 nT at 19:55 UT 15 Jul | wind peaks 1137 km/s 22:05 UT 15 Jul | Kp 9 from 18:35 UT 15 Jul | SYM-H min -326 nT at 21:55 UT 15 Jul | Bz below -10 nT for 6 h
storms.label: Bastille Day 2000
talking_points: WATCH: the CME shock from the X5.7 flare hits L1 about 14:37 UT on 15 Jul - the pressure jumps roughly tenfold and the magnetopause and bow shock crush inward within a step
PHYSICS: Bz swings to about -60 nT. Southward IMF reconnects at the nose, dayside field lines peel back into the tail - watch the tail lines stretch and the oval expand
IMPACT: Kp 9, Dst about -300 nT. Aurora seen as far south as Texas - the ASCA X-ray satellite lost attitude control and never observed again, radio and GPS were disrupted
storms.title: Bastille Day Storm - July 2000 (1140 km/s)
storms.why: Two magnetic clouds and their shocks drive the boundary far inside its usual stand.

storms.key_moments: KEY MOMENTS: shock 08:45 UT 20 Nov (6 -> 12 nPa) | Bz min -52 nT at 15:55 UT 20 Nov | wind peaks 750 km/s 11:25 UT 20 Nov | Kp 8.7 from 15:35 UT 20 Nov | SYM-H min -485 nT at 18:15 UT 20 Nov | Bz below -10 nT for 13 h
storms.label: Nov 2003 superstorm
talking_points: WATCH: not the fastest wind (about 700 km/s) - a magnetic cloud arriving on 20 Nov holds Bz near -50 nT for hours. Sustained southward field, not speed, drives this storm
PHYSICS: hours of steady southward Bz keep dayside reconnection running - the tail loads and the ring current deepens to the cycle record SYM-H near -490 nT
IMPACT: Kp 9-, the deepest storm of solar cycle 23 by Dst (-422 nT). Aurora reported from Texas, Florida and the Mediterranean
storms.title: November 2003 Superstorm (SYM-H -490 nT)
storms.why: The largest geomagnetic storm of solar cycle 23.

storms.key_moments: KEY MOMENTS: shock 18:35 UT 10 May (13 -> 44 nPa) | Bz min -44 nT at 00:35 UT 11 May | wind peaks 1022 km/s 01:25 UT 12 May | Kp 9 from 00:35 UT 11 May | SYM-H min -498 nT at 02:15 UT 11 May | Bz below -10 nT for 18 h
storms.label: Gannon May 2024
talking_points: WATCH: from about 16:30 UT on 10 May several CMEs from active region 13664 arrive stacked - repeated pressure jumps and Bz dips as each one hits
PHYSICS: back-to-back CMEs merge, so southward Bz keeps returning - each dip re-opens the dayside and pumps the tail, and the oval reaches mid-latitudes
IMPACT: G5, Kp 9, Dst about -410 nT - the strongest storm in about 20 years. Aurora photographed from Mexico, Puerto Rico and southern Europe, farm GPS knocked out at planting time
storms.title: Gannon Storm - May 2024 (Kp 9)
storms.why: The first severe (G5) storm in two decades.

storms.key_moments: KEY MOMENTS: shock 15:35 UT 10 Oct (8 -> 22 nPa) | Bz min -46 nT at 22:45 UT 10 Oct | wind peaks 816 km/s 06:55 UT 11 Oct | Kp 8.7 from 21:35 UT 10 Oct | SYM-H min -339 nT at 01:45 UT 11 Oct | Bz below -10 nT for 15 h
storms.label: Oct 2024 G4
talking_points: WATCH: the CME from the X1.8 flare of 8-9 Oct arrives about 15:15 UT on 10 Oct as one sharp shock - a clean single-hit storm to compare with May's stacked arrivals
PHYSICS: Bz near -40 nT for a shorter spell than in May - watch how quickly the magnetopause rebounds once Bz turns north again
IMPACT: G4 severe, Kp 9-, Dst about -333 nT - the second strongest storm of cycle 25 so far, and it arrived in the days after Hurricane Milton
storms.title: October 2024 G4 Storm (aurora to the Gulf Coast)
storms.why: Sympathetic eruptions; aurora reached the Gulf Coast.
